options: A visual and logical representation of how tasks, operations or computations are executed in a system, showing their order and dependencies
A chart of how long each server has been running
A list of employees and their managers
A pie chart of CPU usage
A table of database permissions
questions.explanation: An Execution Graph shows the order in which activities run and how they depend on one another.

questions.stem: In a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG), what does 'acyclic' mean?
options: Tasks may run in any order
The graph does not loop back on itself
Every task runs twice
The graph has no edges
Tasks always run in parallel
questions.explanation: 'Directed' means tasks move in one direction and 'acyclic' means the graph does not loop back on itself; once a task finishes the flow moves forward.

questions.stem: Which single question does an execution graph answer, in simple terms?
options: How much does each task cost?
Who wrote each task?
What runs first, what runs next and what depends on what?
Where is the data physically stored?
Which programming language is fastest?
questions.explanation: An execution graph answers one important question: what runs first, what runs next and what depends on what.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as something an execution graph helps systems do?
options: Understand task dependencies
Run independent tasks in parallel
Recover from failures
Choose the cheapest cloud provider
Track processing stages
questions.explanation: Execution graphs help systems understand dependencies, optimise performance, run independent tasks in parallel, recover from failures and track processing stages.

questions.stem: When a job is submitted to a distributed processing engine, what does the system do before executing it?
options: It runs each line of code immediately in the order written
It sends the code to a human reviewer
It converts the code into a relational table
It compresses the code to save memory
It builds an execution plan, which is converted into an execution graph
questions.explanation: The system does not execute each line immediately; it builds an execution plan and converts it into an execution graph.

questions.stem: In an execution graph, what do the nodes and edges represent?
options: Nodes are tasks or transformations; edges are dependencies between tasks
Nodes are servers; edges are network cables
Nodes are users; edges are permissions
Nodes are tables; edges are foreign keys
Nodes are files; edges are folders
questions.explanation: Each node in an execution graph represents a task or transformation and each edge represents a dependency between tasks.

questions.stem: In the pipeline Read Data, Filter Rows, Aggregate Results, Write Output, when can the Aggregate Results step start?
options: At any time, since all steps are independent
Only after the Filter Rows step it depends on has finished
Before Read Data, to save time
Simultaneously with Write Output
Only after Write Output has completed
questions.explanation: If one step depends on another, it cannot start until the previous one finishes; only independent tasks may run at the same time.

questions.stem: In the school project example of an execution graph, which task can run in parallel with writing notes?
options: Presenting to the class
Collecting information from books
A friend drawing pictures for the poster
Creating the poster
Nothing; every step must wait
questions.explanation: While you write notes, your friend can draw pictures for the poster, showing that some work can happen at the same time.

questions.stem: Why are execution graphs especially important in distributed environments?
options: Because distributed systems have no dependencies
Because they replace the need for code
Because they store the data itself
Because multiple machines process data simultaneously and need tasks ordered correctly
Because they prevent any task from running in parallel
questions.explanation: Execution graphs are especially important where multiple machines process data simultaneously, ensuring correct order and enabling parallel work.

questions.stem: Which statement best captures the key idea of an Execution Graph?
options: It is only a decorative diagram for documentation
It is a type of relational database
It replaces data engineers
It guarantees that tasks never fail
It is how modern data systems organise and optimise work, ensuring correct order, parallel processing and dependency management
questions.explanation: An Execution Graph is not just a diagram: it is how modern data systems organise and optimise work, ensuring correct order and parallelism.
